name: Organizational drift

subjectOf.text: The longevity of a DAO depends on its ability to maintain the fluidity and decentralized order that existed in the DAO's initial stages.
subjectOf.abstract: The longevity of DAOs depends on their ability to maintain the fluidity and decentralized order that was possible in the initial stages of the DAO.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations – Internal Governance and External Legal Design (2020). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3652481

subjectOf.text: Absent continual effort to maintain decentralized order, the very values that initially unite DAO members tend to produce ever tighter and more complex hierarchical structures inside the DAO, ending in a fully centralized tree structure.
subjectOf.abstract: Without continual efforts to maintain decentralized order, values that initially unite DAO members have a tendency to result in ever tighter and complex hierarchical structures in the DAO.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations – Internal Governance and External Legal Design (2020). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3652481
scope_conditions: no ongoing effort is made to preserve decentralized order
